title: Elodie and the Provision
premise: Riverboat captain Jude Blackwood hauls a sealed chest salvaged from the flooded wreck of a vanished nation upriver to sell, only to find its contents — proof of a massacre her own government helped bury — make her a target for both the state and the survivors' descendants. Sheltering through monsoon season in a dying river town with Elodie Vasseur, an archivist who claims the chest by bloodright, Jude must choose between selling out and standing witness. When the glacier calving opens the high route for one brief week, they run the rapids together, delivering the truth to the last free press beyond the pass. Jude loses her boat and her anonymity but gains, at last, a reason to be found.
about_author: Ulyana Whitlock is a former barge hand turned novelist who writes adventure stories set on contested waterways. She lives half the year aboard a restored sternwheeler and claims she still dreams in river miles.

chapters.title: The River Keeps What It Is Given
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Dredging sandbars after a flood, her crew snags a lead-lined chest stamped with the seal of Vaskaria, a nation erased from maps twenty years ago. Jude wants to throw it back; her deckhand quietly photographs it. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Flashback woven into present: why she left her old life measuring days in river miles instead of years, and how invisibility became her religion. The chest sits locked in her hold like a debt. Beat: the cost of hiding.

chapters.title: A Stranger with a Ledger
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At the trading post of Graywater Bend, archivist Elodie Vasseur recognizes the seal from a photograph and confronts Jude, claiming the chest holds her family's confiscated archive. She offers passage money; Jude refuses. Beat: collision of agendas.

chapters.title: The Buyer Who Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A government surveyor offers triple value for the chest, no questions, no paperwork — and mentions Jude's real name, which no one on this river knows. She realizes staying invisible was always someone else's arrangement. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Cast Off in Bad Weather
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude slips her moorings at night with Elodie stowed aboard, heading upriver toward the mountain pass before monsoon closes it. Her hull takes hidden damage on a submerged fence line. Beat: flight with a ticking clock.

chapters.title: What the Chest Weighs
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Trapped below decks by rain, Elodie picks the lock and shows Jude the contents: manifests, photographs, orders bearing signatures that still hold office. Jude reads them twice and says nothing. Beat: loyalty to country begins cracking against truth.

chapters.title: The Leaking Hold
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The damaged seam gives way; they beach at the drowned town of Meridian Flats, where the river swallowed a whole community during the war. Elodie recognizes names on drowned doorposts. Beat: grief as shared ground.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Rain pins them in Meridian Flats for weeks. They repair the hull badly, argue about everything, and begin telling each other true things. A patrol skiff passes downstream, asking after a captain named Blackwood. Beat: intimacy growing inside danger.

chapters.title: The Man from the Survey Office
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The surveyor finds them anyway — he has been tracking the chest since it surfaced. He offers Jude amnesty and her old name back if she surrenders it and forgets Elodie. Beat: temptation made personal.

chapters.title: Belonging to No One
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie confesses she isn't just an heir; she was sent by the survivor network, and using Jude was part of the plan. Jude walks out into the rain. Beat: betrayal cutting deepest because trust had become real.

chapters.title: Cold Camp
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Alone, Jude drafts a letter surrendering the chest, then burns it unread by anyone but herself. She returns not for Elodie but because the truth now belongs to her too. Beat: choice over circumstance.

chapters.title: Repairing More Than the Boat
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Awkward, wordless reconciliation over caulking and engine work. Elodie admits what she withheld; Jude admits she'd have done the same. They plan the run to the pass together, honestly this time. Beat: love rebuilt on terms, not need.

chapters.title: The Patrol Comes Upstream
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Two gunboats seal the lower river. Their only route is the high channel through calving country — open for one week when the glacier sheds its winter face. Beat: the trap closing forces the gamble.

chapters.title: Smugglers of Meridian Flats
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The town's few remaining residents — ferrymen, a nun, a boy who knows every side channel — agree to help, having lost their own history to the same hands. Beat: belonging found among the discarded.

chapters.title: Running the Fence Line
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A night dash past the gunboats using the boy's channels; a near-ramming, a decoy raft, a scraped hull. They clear the cordon but lose their fuel cache. Beat: triumph shadowed by dwindling odds.

chapters.title: The Glacier Road
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They enter the calving corridor: ice groaning, spray like gunfire, a route that exists for days, not seasons. Elodie reads aloud from the archive as they go, making the dead passengers of the story present. Beat: awe and dread braided.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The glacier sheds a wall of ice; the wave swamps the boat. Jude saves the chest before the engine, then Elodie, nearly losing both. They limp into the far shallows, boat dying beneath them. Beat: sacrifice made literal.

chapters.title: What Was Worth Saving
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Wrecked ashore below the pass, they carry the chest on foot. Jude admits the boat was never the point — the miles were how she avoided arriving anywhere. Beat: identity surrendered and reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Last Free Press
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Over the pass, in a border town of exiles, they deliver the archive to a printing house that has waited twenty years for it. The surveyor arrives unarmed, out of jurisdiction, and can only watch. Beat: victory without vengeance.

chapters.title: Witnesses
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The documents go out on wire and newsprint; signatures fall; inquiries open. Elodie asks Jude to stay and help rebuild the record. Jude, whose face is now known everywhere, hesitates. Beat: visibility as a new kind of courage.

chapters.title: A New Route
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Instead of hiding, Jude buys a share in a ferry running the reopened pass road — a boat with a name on it, and hers beside Elodie's in the registry. Beat: choosing to be found.

chapters.title: Elodie and the Provision
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, epilogue. One year later, the two of them run supplies and printed truth upriver to towns still learning what happened. The provision — the promise they made each other in the rain at Meridian Flats — holds. Beat: love and duty reconciled, the river carrying both.
